LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 11 picks, including the Jaguars to handle the Giants on the road Imagn Images Stacking winning weeks is always a good feeling when it comes to picking NFL games . I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. Pick: Texans 30, Colts 27 Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Stroud in desperate need of a win at home against Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts. These teams are in two different places in 2026, yet they both only have three wins through the first 10 weeks of the season. Indianapolis traded away several key players at the deadline, including Josh Downs, Keenan Allen, DeForest Buckner, and Quenton Nelson, as the team simply doesn't have the same juice that it did to open the 2025 campaign. Despite that, the Colts have a win over Houston in 2026, and the Texans have struggled against just about everyone this season. Houston is 3-6 through nine games, losing on the road against the Cleveland Browns in Week 10. The Texans blew a 17-0 lead in that matchup, struggling mightily on offense in the second half. While C.J. Stroud has played well in the 2026 season, the Houston defense has not lived up to expectations after it finished No. 1 in EPA/Play during the 2025 campaign. Oddsmakers still have the Texans favored by 12.5 points at home in this AFC South battle. Can Houston get back on track and keep its slim playoff hopes alive? A win on Thursday would go a long way to getting the Texans back in the mix for the No. 7 seed in the AFC. All week long, the SI Betting team shared their favorite picks, player props and predictions for this AFC South matchup. Here's a breakdown of some of our favorites to get you ready to bet on the first primetime matchup in Week 11 of the NFL season. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Colts vs. Texans Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Indianapolis Colts-Houston Texans OVER 44.5 (-105) – Iain MacMillan Jonathan Taylor OVER 49.5 Rushing Yards (-114) – Peter Dewey Nico Collins Anytime TD (-105) – Peter Dewey Tank Dell OVER 2.5 Receptions (-125) – Peter Dewey All season long, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shares his favorite bet for every game in his Road to 272 column . For Thursday Night Football in Week 11, he’s taking the OVER between these AFC South teams: With the spread in the double digits, I have no interest in backing either team. Instead, I'm going to take the OVER. The Texans' offense has been their strength this season. They're now ninth in the league in EPA per play and fourth in that metric since Week 4. C.J. Stroud has also been phenomenal, ranking inside the top eight in almost every quarterback metric since Week 4. Now they'll get to feast against a horrific Colts defense that's 21st in opponent EPA per play. Of course, it's hard to trust the Colts' offense, but it's time for us to continue to assume that the Houston offense is going to turn things around and become the elite unit it was the past few seasons. The biggest red flag in this game is that they're 22nd in opponent rush EPA and 27th in opponent rush success rate, which will feed directly into the Colts' offensive strength with Jonathan Taylor. Jonathan Taylor has seen his snap share dip a bit in recent weeks – playing less than 70 percent of the offensive plays in four games in a row – yet he’s still handled a ton of touches for Indy. Taylor carried the ball 13 times for 46 yards in Week 9 against Dallas and 16 times for 83 yards in Week 10 against Miami. He had 23 carries and cleared this prop in Week 3 against Houston, which is 20th in EPA/Rush and allowing 4.0 yards per carry this season. The Colts star has at least 50 rushing yards in seven of his 10 games this season, picking up at least 45 rushing yards in nine of his games. Taylor is still the safest bet to go off for an Indy team that moved on from both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the trade deadline. Houston wideout Nico Collins has found the end zone in back-to-back weeks, and he has five touchdowns in seven appearances in the 2026 season. The clear No. 1 option for this Houston offense through the air, Collins has already seen 55 targets from C.J. Stroud, reeling in 37 of them for 478 yards. He was targeted 16 times in the loss to Cleveland in Week 10, and with the Houston running game struggling in 2026, I expect the offense to rely on Stroud throwing the ball on Thursday. The Colts have allowed 17 passing touchdowns this season, but Collins missed the first meeting against them with an injury. I think he makes his presence felt on Thursday night and scores for the third game in a row. After missing all of last season and the start of the 2026 season recovering from a brutal knee injury, Tank Dell is back – and thriving – with Stroud at quarterback. Dell and Stroud have some great chemistry in their time together in the NFL, and the young receiver has played just under 50 percent of the offensive snaps in back-to-back weeks. In Week 9, Dell had four grabs for 105 yards and a score, receiving nine targets from Stroud. He then followed that up with a three-catch game (on four targets) against Cleveland. Dell isn’t going to lead this receiver room in snaps, but he’s getting looks from Stroud when he’s out there and is now facing a defense that is 18th in EPA/Pass, allowing the sixth-most passing yards in the league. away.headline: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts
away.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
away.blurb: Wide receiver Chris Bell has been limited in practice this week with a knee issue. Hafley said he would not practice on Friday and is doubtful, but he has not been ruled out. Hafley said Bell got hit in the leg during practice and it did not have to do with his prior knee injury. Hafley said he expects Chop Robinson and Josh Uche to step up in defensive lineman Zach Sieler's absence . Sieler is out for the season after season-ending biceps surgery. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts Miami Dolphins All-Pro center Aaron Brewer remains in concussion protocol and will not play against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. Hafley also said his new quarterback has a "very calm confidence" about him. "He's got a quiet leadership about him. He's got a confidence to him. He's very calm in the huddle. And he seems to be grasping everything really well," Hafley said. "I think he's done a really good job in the two practices that we've had. (Friday's) a big day again, getting more in the red zone and polishing up some stuff. "But again, this will be a process, right? I'm not going to expect him to look perfect. There's going to be hopefully some really good moments for him and then there's going to be some that we're going to have to continue to grow in these next games. But I'm excited for him and I appreciate how he's worked, attacked the game plan and how he's kind of communicating and developing chemistry with the players around him in the huddle." "The way Chop's playing and really practicing, I think he's a great example of what it's supposed to look like," Hafley said. "And I think he's going to grow into one of those roles."

away.headline: Colts rule out 5 players ahead of primetime matchup with Texans
away.blurb: The Colts have ruled out five players ahead of Thursday night’s primetime Week 11 road game against the Texans , including three starters. Travis, missing his second straight game due to a knee injury, was banged up entering the Colts’ Week 9 home game but played. He missed all three of the team’s practices leading up to Week 10 and was ruled out prior to the game. Travis was estimated to have missed all three of the team’s practices -- had they been held this week -- as Colts head coach Shane Steichen opted for walkthrus. The Colts will also be without starting cornerback Charvarius Ward , who left Sunday’s game with what was initially described as a shin injury. Ward has since been an estimated DNP throughout the team’s three walkthrus this week with a knee injury. Despite several injuries cropping up for Ward since the summer, this will be his first missed game of the year. Defensive tackle Jerry Tillery (calf) and tight end Will Mallory (hamstring) will both miss their second consecutive game for the Colts. The Colts have also listed four players, including starting cornerback Sauce Gardner , questionable. Gardner left Sunday’s game with an injury to the same left calf that held him out of Week 7 earlier this year and lost him four full games and parts of two more in the back-half of 2025. He was estimated to have missed all three practices this week. Starting long snapper Luke Rhodes , who missed just his second game in nearly a decade in Indianapolis, is also questionable with a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 9 that cost him all three practices last week and ruled him out for Week 10. Rhodes was an estimated non-participant Monday but was limited Tuesday and Wednesday this week, a sign he’s moving in the right direction. Starting slot receiver and return man Anthony Gould (toe) is questionable, though he’s also trending in the right direction. Gould was limited in the team’s first two estimated practice reports this week, but he was listed as a full participant Wednesday. Offensive tackle Charlie Heck will not travel with the team to Houston on Wednesday due to personal reasons, and he’s also listed as questionable. Raimann suffered a concussion early in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins , and with a short week, progressing through the NFL’s concussion protocol was an unlikely scenario. home.blurb: Is Deshaun Watson Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Texans vs. Browns in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE The Cleveland Browns will get their starting quarterback back in action in Week 10 against the Houston Texans, as Deshaun Watson is off the injury report and set to start. Watson (concussion) missed the team's Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints, though backup Shedeur Sanders played pretty decently in his place. Sanders helped get the Browns to overtime, where they lost on a two-point attempt. The second-year quarterback finished the day with 297 passing yards and two scores, carrying the ball for 28 yards on 10 attempts as well. Still, Todd Monken named Watson the starter for Week 10, as the veteran has led the team to a 5-3 record in eight starts with five fourth quarter comeback wins. In the 2026 season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven scores and three interceptions. He's also carried the ball 51 times for 217 yards and a score. He's playing a revenge game against his former team -- Houston -- in Week 10. Even with Watson back, oddsmakers aren't buying the 5-4 Browns in this matchup. They are 4.5-point underdogs at home in the latest odds at DraftKings , even though they have a better record than an underachieving Houston team so far in 2026. Watson is looking to have a big game to keep the starting job, as it's possible the Browns could turn back to Sanders if things go south. Cleveland is still in the playoff picture in the AFC, but it has taken a step back with two straight losses to Pittsburgh and New Orleans. home.headline: Colts rule out 5 players ahead of primetime matchup with Texans
home.blurb: The Colts have ruled out five players ahead of Thursday night’s primetime Week 11 road game against the Texans , including three starters. Travis, missing his second straight game due to a knee injury, was banged up entering the Colts’ Week 9 home game but played. He missed all three of the team’s practices leading up to Week 10 and was ruled out prior to the game. Travis was estimated to have missed all three of the team’s practices -- had they been held this week -- as Colts head coach Shane Steichen opted for walkthrus. The Colts will also be without starting cornerback Charvarius Ward , who left Sunday’s game with what was initially described as a shin injury. Ward has since been an estimated DNP throughout the team’s three walkthrus this week with a knee injury. Despite several injuries cropping up for Ward since the summer, this will be his first missed game of the year. Defensive tackle Jerry Tillery (calf) and tight end Will Mallory (hamstring) will both miss their second consecutive game for the Colts. The Colts have also listed four players, including starting cornerback Sauce Gardner , questionable. Gardner left Sunday’s game with an injury to the same left calf that held him out of Week 7 earlier this year and lost him four full games and parts of two more in the back-half of 2025. He was estimated to have missed all three practices this week. Starting long snapper Luke Rhodes , who missed just his second game in nearly a decade in Indianapolis, is also questionable with a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 9 that cost him all three practices last week and ruled him out for Week 10. Rhodes was an estimated non-participant Monday but was limited Tuesday and Wednesday this week, a sign he’s moving in the right direction. Starting slot receiver and return man Anthony Gould (toe) is questionable, though he’s also trending in the right direction. Gould was limited in the team’s first two estimated practice reports this week, but he was listed as a full participant Wednesday. Offensive tackle Charlie Heck will not travel with the team to Houston on Wednesday due to personal reasons, and he’s also listed as questionable. Raimann suffered a concussion early in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins , and with a short week, progressing through the NFL’s concussion protocol was an unlikely scenario. More importantly, it showed Americans that television cartoons can be relished by adults. So I'm hoping you'll catch my meaning when I use a famous Simpsons quote to personify the Buffalo Bills . The NFL team that famously lost four straight Super Bowls in the 1990s is enjoying a Milhouse moment right now. Milhouse Van Houten is Bart Simpson's lovably awkward and loyal best friend. So, maybe this Milhouse moment is sticking around. Bills vs. Dolphins odds (Odds as of Monday afternoon) The Bills are 16.5-point favorites. The over/under is 45.5 points. Getty Cole Shelton · HEAVY Tue, November 17, 2026 at 5:10 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Bills predicted to promote Tre'Davious White. Getty The Buffalo Bills could rely on a veteran cornerback against the Miami Dolphins. Buffalo is coming off a road win over the New York Jets to improve to 8-1 and is atop the AFC. The Bills have been playing great, but they did suffer some key injuries in the win, which could mean the team has to make some roster moves. Buffalo is set to host the Dolphins on Sunday. Buffalo Bills Predicted to Promote Tre'Davious White GettyBills predicted to promote Tre'Davious White. In the Bills' win over the Jets, starting cornerback Christian Benford suffered an injury, which is a bit of a concern. However, if Benford can't go, Bills reporter Joe Buscagalia of The Athletic believes the team will elevate Tre'Davious White from the practice squad. "Tre'Davious White is on the practice squad, and this is why the Bills brought him back in the first place," Buscagalia wrote . "That's also why they decided against going after another veteran cornerback in the trade market. … "If Benford has to miss any time, the Bills might need White to play as early as next week. And if it goes well enough, maybe even earn a bigger role as the year goes on." White would be entering his 11th NFL season. He signed with Buffalo's practice squad during the year as he wanted to return after starting 16 games and playing well a year ago. Buffalo selected White in the first round of the 2017 NFL Draft, and he became a lockdown corner. Although he's no longer the No. 1 cornerback he once was, he can add some depth to the cornerback room if Benford is out. White Believes He's Ready to Play White has been on the Bills' practice squad and could get his first elevation against the Dolphins on Sunday. The veteran cornerback spoke to The Athletic and admitted he's feeling good and ready to play. "Everybody's been telling me I look good, so there it is. You know, I always leave it to my teammates and my peers," the 31-year-old said. "I always say it like, 'Hey, you see me out there and I look like I'm walking, just tell me to hang it up.' And nobody told me to hang it up yet, Joe, so I'm good, man, I feel like I am good." White, meanwhile, has also been mentoring rookie Davison Igbinosun and sophomore Maxwell Hairston. It's a different role for White, but along with mentoring, he knows he's here to play. "This ain't have to be what it was; this is what I chose," White said. "You know what I mean? I could have been anywhere else on a team, on a 53, playing right now, but I'm a Bill. … I mean, it's bigger than me, man." "I know I can go out there and play right now. Movement good, body feels good, I know how I can play, but right now my role is to help the young guys out and to be that. But it's hard, being that I just started every game last year, you know what I mean? And played good football. So it's like, ' Ahh .' But I'm going to trust the process, and I'm gonna be here to cheer the guys on. But as I'm doing it, I'm definitely preparing to play, too." The Bills are 8-1. away.headline: Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report
away.blurb: The only other player who has now been hit with a DNP (did not participate) is rookie wide receiver Chris Bell. Bell is still dealing with a knee injury, which is connected to his torn ACL that he suffered at the end of his collegiate career in 2025. Bell has appeared on the injury report off and on since returning in Week 1 to play, and now he was downgraded from a limited participant on Wednesday to DNP on Thursday. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee ), edge Malik Herring (neck), tight end Will Kacmarek (quad/knee), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) were all limited. Some good news in these listed players is that Kacmarek was upgraded to limited after missing Thursday's practice. Baker also remains limited, which could mean that he is not yet ready to play. The cornerback has made his return to practice after not playing in 2026 due to suffering a knee injury in training camp. There is still a chance that Baker could play, but the usual case is that players who remain limited likely need a week or so more to fully get back to being able to take the field. Wright has been dealing with a quad injury that led to him being ruled out in Week 9. Now, he is set to return against the Colts. Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report (David Brytus-Imagn Images) James Brizuela · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 12, 2026 at 10:22 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Miami Dolphins have released their second injury report of Week 10, and things are not looking good for center Aaron Brewer. Brewer has now missed his second straight practice, as he is currently in concussion protoco l. It is not unlikely that he will suit up against the Indianapolis Colts. The full injury report is as follows: Running back Kaytron Allen (quad), safety Michael Taaffe (wrist), safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), and running back Jaylen Wright (quad) were all full participants yet again. Despite the semblance of a laundry list of injured players, the Dolphins look to be in decent shape. Losing Brewer will be a huge hit to the offense, but Andrew Meyer will be there to step in. Meyer spoke on Thursday about not only learning from "the best center in the league" but also stating that he has the confidence to step in for the Miami offensive line if that is what happens. The Dolphins are looking for their second win of the season, as they will face the struggling Colts. Indianapolis may not be a pushover opponent, but they also got rid of many players at the trade deadline, leaving this to be a potential "easier" matchup for Miami.

away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published 16 hours ago ALAIN POUPART Ala

Travis Etienne is making a bid to come back off of IR from his hamstring injury, and the Saints are getting new injury updates on Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson, too. A couple of practice appearances already suggest Etienne is close — maybe as soon as this week, or maybe next week. Either way, it's big news for the Saints, who have played more than half the season without the guy they signed to be their No. 1 running back. Etienne hadn't been great before being hurt, but his injury definitely made the RB situation more complicated. When Etienne returns, he may not get a giant workload right away as the Saints ease him back in, but expect him to eventually take over the lead in this backfield. Defensive back Kyler Gordon rose as the only one who did not practice. Wide receiver Luther Burden III, running back Kyle Monangai and DB Malik Muhammad emerged as full participants. But he sounds like he's taking his frustrations out after the Titans trade. Even he told The Rich Eisen Show he became shocked by the Titans move. Reyna, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Wed, November 18, 2026 at 10:39 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Chicago Bears ignited their defense by adding All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . Head coach Ben Johnson has raved about the presence of the former Tennessee Titans star. But he landed on the NFL injury report before facing the New Orleans Saints. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Still, Simmons has flexed his impact already on the Bears defensive line. Simmons lured his relentless pass rushing over from Nashville. "I'm on Year 8 here, I was the glue of trying to hold this locker room together," he said. "I tried to give the organization so much on the field, in the locker room, at practice and in the community, and that's why I didn't think it would happen to me. I was pissed off." Yet now he joins a franchise that's won four straight games and shares a 7-2 mark with the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions. Chicago sits at third, though, in the current standings of the NFC North. Meanwhile, the Saints are one game behind in their NFC South race but sit at 3-6 overall. I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. Pick: Texans 30, Colts 27 Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Cowboys in Week 11, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Titans just lost their eighth game in nine tries, but there's a lot to like about where Tennessee stands right now. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As Saleh himself said after the team's latest loss, you aren't going to win allowing 40 points a game. The Titans' previous two opponents have crossed the 40 mark, and Dallas, in spite of their loss, score as much against a better 49ers defense this past week. As Saleh himself said after the team's latest loss, you aren't going to win allowing 40 points a game. The Titans' previous two opponents have crossed the 40 mark, and Dallas, in spite of their loss, score as much against a better 49ers defense this past week. Dallas is a veteran-led group in the middle of a difficult year; their down season can't be compared to that of the Titans, and QB Dak Prescott is sure to run this defense through the ringer. On the road after arguably their worst showing of the year, Saleh's defense has their back against the wall. Prediction: Titans win, 30-27 With that said, I still think the Titans find a way to pull this one out. If the away team can strike a balance between their growing offensive attack and a defense that isn't allowing Dallas to do whatever they want, a close win is in the cards. The Titans have yet to play a full, complete game this year. Even their Week 6 victory over the Indianapolis Colts saw Tennessee trailing 13-0 at halftime. I'm predicting that the Titans get this done, and do so by offering a solid showing through all four quarters. That means a consistent Cam Ward, a defense that bends, but doesn't break, reliable play-calling on either side of the ball, and at least a little good luck on the injury front. A lot has to go right, but this game wouldn't have been seen as winnable only a few short weeks ago. For that reason, I believe the Titans will win it. away.blurb: Jacksonville's trade deadline splashes sitting out against Tennessee Those two additions round out a defensive unit that, when healthy, leaves Jacksonville with no real holes on paper as it chases a championship. A detail that's easy to lose track of at the trade deadline is how bye weeks shake out for traded players. Because teams take their byes at different points on the calendar, a player can get robbed of his bye entirely if his old team hadn't had one yet and his new team already did. On the flip side, some players luck into two. In the case of both Bates and Davis, neither had a bye this season until the Jaguars decided to hold them out against Tennessee. That gives them time to get up to speed mentally and to get some rest and recovery at the midpoint of the season before a push down the stretch, when it matters most for Jacksonville. Robert Saleh should be bringing it up in team meetings on Friday, again on Saturday, and in any meeting he has before kickoff on Sunday. The message writes itself: these guys don't respect you enough to deploy the starters they just went out and paid big for. They don't think they need them. That's how little they think of you. That gap gets wider when you look at the star power Tennessee will be missing. Rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate has already been ruled out yet again with his shoulder injury. The reporting when he sat out the Cincinnati Bengals game in Week 8 was that the Titans wanted him to roll that absence into the bye week and get roughly three full weeks of rest. He clearly isn't quite ready to come back. Linebackers Anthony Hill and Cody Barton are both ruled out as well. That means Cedric Gray gets a big prove-it week, with Tennessee running thin at the position. The offensive line takes a hit, too. Star left guard Peter Skoronski is out, and neither Fernando Carmona nor swing backup Jackson Slater has returned from the injuries that knocked them out at right guard. So the Titans will be without either of their starting guards. Atonio Mafi, who has held down right guard admirably, likely stays on the right side, and yet another depth player (technically guard No. 5 on the depth chart) will step in on the left, whoever Tennessee deems worthy of the role. home.headline: What’s Up With the Cowboys’ Injuries? Tough Report Released Wednesday
home.blurb: Seven Dallas Cowboys players did not practice Wednesday, including starters Tyler Booker, DaRon Bland and Jake Ferguson, four days before the 1-8 Tennessee Titans arrive at AT&T Stadium. The DNP list consisted of tight end Ferguson (knee and ankle), cornerback Bland (ankle), right guard Booker (ankle), outside linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku (ankle), safety P.J. Locke (concussion) and wide receiver Jonathan Mingo (ankle). Outside linebacker Von Miller also sat out, but the report lists his absence as a veteran rest day, not an injury. No game designations have been issued — yet. Booker, a 2025 first-round pick, had started every game at right guard with an 84.8 Pro Football Focus grade . Sprains like his typically sideline players four to six weeks , according to NFL Network, though Booker could return within four. T.J. Bass steps in at right guard. Bland's sprain is in the opposite ankle from the one that limited him in practice last week. Cobie Durant took over most outside cornerback work after he left. Placing either on injured reserve would cost four games, and Dallas has used most of its eight return designations this season. So who plays? Ferguson is not expected to play against Tennessee , and Booker and Bland are expected to miss multiple weeks. Miller, listed for rest only, is expected to be available, and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (ankle and foot) practiced fully. Locke, Ezeiruaku and Mingo remain uncertain until Friday's report. home.blurb: The biggest absences included cornerback DaRon Bland, right guard Tyler Booker and tight end Jake Ferguson. All three missed practice with injuries suffered during or around the Cowboys' loss to San Francisco. Bland and Booker both dealt with ankle injuries after going down during Sunday's game. “Booker and Bland both suffered high ankle sprains in Sunday's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Bland went down on San Francisco's first touchdown drive while tackling Deebo Samuel Sr., and Booker followed later in the first half. Neither returned,” Jonathan Vankin of Heavy wrote. Ferguson was another major concern. The tight end suffered PCL and MCL sprains in his left knee and was expected to miss multiple weeks, according to head coach Brian Schottenheimer. He had recorded four touchdown catches this season, making his absence another setback for Dak Prescott's offense. Linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku, safety P.J. Locke and wide receiver Jonathan Mingo joined them on the list of players who did not practice. Locke was dealing with a concussion, while Ezeiruaku and Mingo had ankle injuries. Dallas gets some positive injury updates before Titans clash Not every update goes against the Cowboys. Safety Jalen Thompson returned to practice for the first time since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3. Dallas opened his 21-day practice window, allowing him to begin working toward a return. He took part in a limited session alongside fellow safety Juanyeh Thomas, who was managing a hamstring issue. Safety Malik Hooker, linebacker James Houston, cornerback Joey Porter Jr., cornerback Devin Moore and defensive tackle Otito Ogbonnia all practiced fully despite appearing on the injury report. Dallas needed those defensive options after allowing 584 total yards and 46 points against San Francisco. The team had already made a change in its defensive setup by handing play-calling duties to Mike Pettine after taking them away from Christian Parker. Yours truly gave out the Los Angeles Chargers to upset the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football in last week's upset picks roundtable , and they came through for us. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 11 Upset Pick Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+215) vs. Detroit Lions It didn’t go well for me last week betting against the Lions. But this time it will be different! Remember, a broken clock is right twice a day. Anyway, Detroit will have a few challenges in this one, including facing a tough Tampa Bay defense a week after having to play a game in Germany. The Lions’ explosive offense had trouble generating points against Green Bay, Minnesota, and Miami (the Dolphins!) before bouncing back against the Patriots last week. Perhaps Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles could use some of those blueprints to slow down star running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Also, this will be the Lions’ first game without star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who sustained a season-ending knee injury against the Patriots. Peter Dewey Week 11 Upset Pick Baltimore Ravens (+114) vs. Carolina Panthers If you’re going to make a case for an upset this week where there are five teams favored by double digits, I don’t mind targeting the Baltimore Ravens in their clash with the Carolina Panthers. Carolina barely came away with a win over a bad New Orleans team in Week 10, and it remains pretty banged up on both sides of the ball. The Panthers are a top-10 team in the league in EPA/Play on offense, but they’re in the middle of the pack in EPA/Play on the defensive side of the ball. Carolina is also allowing 4.4 yards per carry on the ground, so this could be the week Derrick Henry gets going. The Ravens are coming off a pretty huge loss at home against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night, but Jacoby Brissett wasn’t bad in that matchup, and he may have led this Baltimore team to a win had Zay Flowers not lost a costly fumble late in the fourth quarter. I don’t think that any team in the NFC South should be trusted as a favorite, as the division as a whole is just 4-17 against the AFC North over the last four seasons and 63-111 overall against non-NFC South teams during that stretch. Iain MacMillan Week 11 Upset Pick The Lions' already bad and injured defense continues to take big hits. Now it's their star pass-rusher, Aidan Hutchinson, who is out for the season after celebrating a sack against the Patriots on Sunday. He joins a list that includes D.J. Reed, Kerby Joseph, Devin White, and Jack Campbell, who are on the injured list. It's enough to convince me that now is the time to sell your Lions' stock. Detroit now has to take on a Buccaneers team that's fresh off a BYE week, and that ranks in the top five in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. While the Lions' offense is certainly elite, they're going to struggle to rack up the amount of points they need to aid their limping defense. Baker Mayfield's injury status is up in the air, which could make this bet tough to win, but if he plays, we're in a great spot. Even if he doesn't, Tampa Bay can win this game with their defense and rushing attack alone. They're my upset pick of the week. Baker Mayfield (ankle/foot) officially did not practice on Wednesday, an ominous sign for his status in Week 11 against the Detroit Lions. Mayfield reportedly was injured in Week 9 against the Chicago Bears, and it appears he hasn't improved enough -- even with the Bucs' bye in Week 10 -- to practice to start this week. That sets undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels up to make his fourth start of the season, even though Mayfield reportedly is pushing to play. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, Mayfield is "probably a long shot" to suit up on Sunday. Fowler: Baker Mayfield (foot, ankle) "probably a long shot" to play Week 11. Mayfield will push to get ready and play this week so the Bucs aren't ruling out the possibility he plays but there's more optimism about him playing in the Week 12 divisional matchup against Panthers. pic.twitter.com/Ih0jaNdPDF Mayfield's injury has caused a ton of movement in the odds for this game -- all in the Lions' favor. Tampa Bay has opened up as a 5.5-point underdog at DraftKings against the Lions and was set at +195 to pick up a road win. The Bucs then shifted to 6.5-point underdogs on Tuesday and have continued to move to seven-point underdogs on Thursday. Not only that, but Tampa Bay is just +270 on the moneyline, which translates to a 27.03 percent chance to win, now that Mayfield missed Wednesday's practice. The Bucs have survived without Mayfield this season, winning one of Daniels' three starts, yet the undrafted rookie is far from an elite quarterback. He'll have to put up points against a Lions offense that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play and fourth in success rate. This season in five appearances (three starts), Daniels has 61.2 percent of his passes for 501 yards, three scores and five picks. He's also added 22 carries for 123 yards on the ground. Mayfield honestly hasn't been much better, completing 60.6 percent of his passes for 922 yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions in his six games. If Mayfield is unable to practice on Thursday as well, it's possible oddsmakers will fully adjust this line with the notion that Daniels will start. Tampa Bay is currently 3-6 and behind the Carolina Panthers in the NFC South race. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. picks.headline: Lions preview: Breaking down Buccaneers’ offensive, defensive schemes
picks.blurb: Lions preview: Breaking down Buccaneers’ offensive, defensive schemes - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Giannis red hot vs. Bucks Boone's trade charts Cowboys DC latest Lions preview: Breaking down Buccaneers’ offensive, defensive schemes DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 20: Todd Bowles head coach of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Dan Campbell head coach of the Detroit Lions shake hands after the game at Ford Field on October 20, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images Erik Schlitt · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions and Tampa Bay Buccaneers will square off in a Week 11 NFC showdown. Lions coach Dan Campbell and Bucs coach Todd Bowles have a long history together—dating back to when Campbell played in Dallas (2005)—and they've gone head-to-head four times in the last three seasons, with Detroit winning three of those matchups. "Tampa Bay Bucs, competitive, physical unit. Known (Buccaneers Head Coach) Todd Bowles a long time. Obviously have got a ton of respect for him and what he's about. And this defense is playing outstanding football. And offensively, they're committed to the run game, time of possession. They're trying to force you into making errors. And really, the last three games, they played some pretty good football." Let's take a closer look at the Bucs' coaching staff, the scheme that they run, and some scouting notes from previously viewed games. Bucs head coach: Todd Bowles NFL coaching seasons: 27 seasons (Bucs, Jets, Cardinals, Eagles, Dolphins, Cowboys, Browns) Head coaching seasons: 10 seasons (Dolphins 2011—interim, Jets 2015-18, Bucs 2022-present) Defensive coordinator seasons : 6 seasons (Eagles 2012, Cardinals 2013-14, Bucs 2019-2021) Influences: Bill Parcells, Mike Zimmer, Mike Nolan, Chuck Pagano, Paul Pasqualoni, Juan Castillo Coached under : Parcells, Bruce Arians, Andy Reid, Tony Soarano, Wade Phillips, Butch Davis, Al Groh Playcaller : Yes (Defense) Offensive coordinator: Zac Robinson NFL coaching seasons : 8 seasons (Bucs, Falcons, Rams) QB seasons in NFL : 4 years (Bengals, Lions, Seahawks, Patriots) Offensive coordinator seasons : 3 seasons (Bucs 2026, Falcons 2024-25) Previous coaching seasons : Passing game coordinator, QB coach, Assistant QB coach, Asst. WR coach Influences: Sean McVay, Bill O'Brien & Tom Brady (Pats), Kyle Shanahan Coached under : McVay, Kevin Stefanski Offensive scheme Passing game : McVay West Coast Running scheme : Shanahan outside zone and gap schemes Staples of scheme : Very similar scheme to what the Bucs have had with Baker Mayfield at QB Robinson comes from the same McVay/Shanahan tree as other former Bucs' OCs, Dave Canales (Panthers HC), Liam Coen (Jaguars HC), and Josh Grizzard (Eagles PGC) Mainly 11 Personnel: 63.3% of the time 12-personnel: 24%, 13-personnel: 8.5%, 21-personnel: 4% More shotgun (53%) than under center (37%), which is a change from previous regimes Staples: Play-action (27.5%, 8th most), pre-snap motion, and bunch formations are staples Balanced approach, pure progression reads, rhythm passing plays Want to attack and push the ball vertically QB (Mayfield, not UDFA Jalon Daniels) has the freedom at the line to check into better plays It's been an up-and-down season for Mayfield, who played in Weeks 1-3, missed Weeks 4-6 with a thumb (throwing hand) injury, returned for Weeks 7-9, and is now injured again (foot) and may not play in this game When Mayfield has played, his numbers have regressed; passer rating of 74.9 (31st in the NFL) In his six games played, he has less than 1,000 total passing yards Mayfield has more interceptions than touchdowns thrown: just 3 TDs and 4 INTs Mayfield has also fumbled six times Bottom three in the NFL in: passing yards, pass yards per play, explosive passing plays, passing success rate Offensive line has done well to mitigate pressures: 107 over nine games (8th fewest) But they've allowed 27 sacks (24th) and a 10.1% sack rate (30th) Mayfield 18 sacks over 6 games; Daniels 9 sacks over 3 games Introduced more balanced zone run concepts; a change from last year's inside zone/downhill approach Outside zone: 22.8%; inside zone: 17.2%; gap/man: 25%; Counters: 18.7% Run game has been very successful No. 1 in the NFL in average rushing yards per game: 163.9; rush yards per play: 5.0; and explosive runs over the last four games: 16.1% Success rate over last four games: 47.4% (5th) EPA per rush: -0.02 (10th) Essentially, they're wearing teams down with consistent success and hitting on big plays in the run game Dan Campbell on the Bucs' offense : "Offensively we'll see what happens with (QB) Baker (Mayfield), but obviously have got a lot of respect for him, what he's capable of, what he's done in this league. Good receivers on the perimeter. Obviously (WR Chris) Godwin (Jr.) and (WR Emeka) Egbuka over there and they got speed with (WR Tez Johnson) 15. (TE Cade) Otton's a solid tight end and this O-line is just an all-day sucker. They'll just keep coming all day long." Campbell on the Bucs' rushing attack : "Bucky (Irving)'s a hell of a back. Honestly, I should have started with him. I mean, this guy is, he really is their lifeblood for what they do offensively in this run game. And this O-line will lean on you, and they're all-day suckers, man. I mean, they will bring it all day long. And he has just got that; he's got a feel. He's got a feel for finding that crease. He understands he's got spatial awareness. He knows when these defenders are closing in on him, he can backdoor it, he can dip under, he can burst back out. And then once you get him into the second level of the defense, he's even more dangerous. So, they want to get him going here. And (RB Kenneth) Gainwell, we know too. I think Gainwell's a damn good back too. Very versatile. So, there's no secret there." Run Game Coordinator/OLB: Larry Foote For three seasons (2022-24), Foote (a Michigan native) served as the Bucs' co-defensive coordinator alongside current Lions defensive line coach Kacy Rodgers, while Bowles maintained play-calling duties. In 2025, the Bucs shifted titles, naming Foote Run Game Coordinator and outside linebackers coach. NFL coaching seasons: 12 seasons (Bucs, Cardinals) LB seasons in NFL : 13 seasons (Cardinals, Steelers, Lions) Roles with Bucs : OLB coach, Co-DC/Passing game coordinator/ILB coach, Run game coordinator/OLB coach Influences: Bruce Arians, Todd Bowles, Dick LeBeau, Jim Schwartz Coached under: Arians, Bowles, Steve Wilks Defensive scheme Base : Attacking 3-4 Coverage : Zone, single-high Staples of scheme : Aggressive, attacking scheme: 2-gapping DL and stand-up pass-rushing OLBs Nickel formations: 67% of the time means a lot of 2-4-5 formations Blitz-heavy: 43.9% (2nd most in the NFL, behind only the Vikings) Utilize blitz to rush the passer and stop the run Very creative blitzer scheme—although there's a lot of tape on Bowles' style/tendencies 3-3 Fire zones, replacement blitzing, Phantom blitzing DL stunts and slants designed to disrupt up front Pressures have declined: 112 through nine games (23rd); pressure rate: 33% (24th) As has sack production: 17 sacks (24th); sack rate: 5% (25th) Zone-heavy (85%), specifically Cover-3: 52% of the time Cover-2: 9%, Cover-4: 24%, Cover-6: 2.5% When in man coverage, it's mainly Cover-1: 9.5%, with some Cover-0 (2.5%) mixed in Bump-and-run coverage approach with corners to stay tight early in route Done well to eliminate explosive passing plays: less than 5% of attempts (No. 1 in the NFL) Done well to slow down explosive run plays: 8% (8th) Fewest rushing yards allowed per game: 79.1 (1st) Rushing yards per play: 3.5 (3rd) EPA per rush: -0.13 (3rd) Success rate over last four games: 41.2% (16th) Dan Campbell on the Bucs' defense: "They've got some impact players, guys that make it very difficult for you. Obviously (NT) Vita Vea there in the middle and (LB) Alex (Anzalone) is playing at a high level. (LB Josiah) Trotter, (S Antoine) Winfield (Jr.). I mean, we can keep going here. (DL Calijah) Kancey and they have got a ton of guys on defense playing really good football." Campbell on the Bucs' rookies making an impact: "Trotter's the best example of that. Every week he gets better and better and better in this case. The key and diagnose and his running, he's downhill and I mean he sees it and he is all out, man. I mean this guy is aggressive. So, he's really growing and he's just the best example of that, but their young guys are growing."

After taking down the Patriots in Germany, the Detroit Lions (7-2) return home to Michigan for a Week 11 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) inside the comfy confines of Ford Field. While the Lions are making the long journey back from Munich, the Bucs are coming off their bye week. The Lions are playing tremendous football right now. They’re currently on a five-game winning streak and are coming off a convincing win overseas, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions - 5.5 points . In the 2026 offseason, the Bucs saw several staple players depart Tampa Bay, including WR Mike Evans, LB LaVonte David, and CB Jamel Dean. The Bucs also saw QB Teddy Bridgewater (before his retirement) and DB Christian Izien leave for the Lions, while signing a handful of former Lions to their current roster, including LB Alex Anzalone, DE Al-Quadin Muhamed, DL A’Shawn Robinson, S Ifeatu Melifonwu, and S Miles Killebrew. After opening the season 0-4, the Bucs are 3-2 over their last five games, including wins over the Cowboys, Panthers, and Falcons, but lost their most recent game to the Chicago Bears. The Bears jumped out to an early 14-0 lead, but after the Bucs intercepted Bears QB Caleb Williams four (!) times, they climbed back into the game. Tampa Bay scored 11 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 24, but Williams got the Bears into field goal range, and Bears kicker Carlos Santos kicked the game-winner as time expired. With that loss, the Bucs have now lost all three games against NFC North teams this season, and the Lions will want to complete the sweep. away.headline: Lions release initial injury report vs. Buccaneers: DJ Reed returns
away.blurb: Starting center Cade Mays (ankle) did not practice. Starting cornerback DJ Reed (hip) returned to practice, but he was a limited participant. Reed has missed each of the Lions' past two games, and the 5-foot-9, 190-pound corner didn't practice either week. Linebacker Joe Bachie (knee), cornerback Khalil Dorsey (ankle), defensive lineman Tyler Lacy (shoulder), cornerback Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder), and running back Sione Vaki (ankle) were also all limited participants. As the Detroit Lions (7-2) gear up for Sunday's showdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6), the team released their initial injury report ahead of the matchup. The Lions activated safety Kerby Joseph on Wednesday. Joseph, who has been working back from a chronic knee injury, was a full participant in the Lions ' initial injury report. away.blurb: Mayfield (foot/right thumb) was held out of Wednesday’s session after suffering an injury to his foot and ankle area during the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Chicago Bears. Cornerback Josh Hayes (knee), tight end Cade Otton (thumb) and left tackle Tristan Wirfs (toe) participated fully. Hayes returned to practice Wednesday, opening his 21-day activation window from injured reserve. For Detroit, center Cade Mays (ankle) was the only player listed as a non-participant. home.headline: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury
home.blurb: "Nothing new," Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game when asked for an update on Hutchinson. "We’ll know more when we get back to the States. But any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out." This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury Initial tests on Aidan Hutchinson’s injured knee showed the Detroit Lions star has a torn ACL, according to a report from NFL Network on Monday, Nov. 16. Hutchinson, 26, had initial tests performed in Germany, where the Lions beat the New England Patriots on Sunday, and will have more done in the United States, the report added. On Good Morning Football, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said, “my understanding, the belief is it’s a torn ACL and more for Aidan Hutchinson.” The injury to Hutchinson occurred in the first quarter of Detroit’s win over the Patriots. Hutchinson sacked quarterback Drake Maye and leapt into the air to celebrate. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right knee. Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side. Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday. If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

picks.headline: Chiefs-Cardinals betting line & prediction: Kansas City’s biggest mismatch yet?
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. Kansas City enters 7-2, while Arizona has lost two straight to fall to 3-7. The betting line lists the Chiefs as 15.5-point favorites over the Cardinals. The prediction picks Kansas City to beat Arizona 33-9 and cover the spread. The Kansas City Chiefs won their second game in a row Sunday when they overpowered the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 , improving to 7-2 on the NFL season. The Arizona Cardinals lost their second straight 34-6 to the Los Angeles Rams to drop to 3-7. Here’s what to know about their matchup on Sunday ... How to watch Cardinals at Chiefs Kickoff: Noon Central Where: Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -15.5 Behind the ARI-KC matchup While the Chiefs were getting back on track by taking care of business against the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons over the past two weeks, the Cardinals have been falling apart at the seams. Sunday’s monumental mismatch starts at the quarterback position, where rookie Carson Beck is expected to make his second career start after completing just 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards and two interceptions against the Rams. Arizona has turned to Beck after trading Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens and watching last year’s Chiefs backup Gardner Minshew tear the UCL in his throwing arm. Understanding the reality of the situation, linebacker Drue Tranquill showed the two-time national champion with Georgia some respect before outlining the problems he may face against a Chiefs defense that has come alive with eight sacks over the last two games. “He’s obviously got winning pedigree — he did it in college,” Tranquill said of Beck. “He’ll get another start under his belt this week in a great environment, so it’s a good opportunity for him, but we’ll have to execute our pre-snap looks, have to execute our game plan in terms of owning our leverage, taking away options he might want to go to early in the down. And then hopefully, as the game progresses, we can get the pass rush going, get them in known passing situations and get them on the ground.” With running back Jeremiyah Love, the No. 3 overall pick, on injured reserve, the Cardinals’ best path to an upset is extending possessions with veteran back Tyler Allgeier and utilizing first-team All-Pro tight end Trey McBride. McBride has managed 78 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns despite Arizona’s struggles. With wide receivers Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Michael Wilson (neck) out for the remainder of the season, that’s left McBride as Beck’s lone viable option. Among Arizona’s available players, tight end Elijah Higgins ranks second on the team in receiving yards with 18 catches for 162 yards. “They’ve got some good tight ends, and so we’ll have to be on it,” Tranquill said. “They’re big, they’re physical, can make contested catches. And so we’ll have to own our leverage and be physical at the top of the stem and not allow them to create separation, and try to get the ball off these guys.” Arizona’s protection has allowed 28 sacks this season — tied for the sixth-most in the league. Meanwhile, Chiefs defensive lineman George Karlaftis enters Sunday with at least one sack in each of his last three games , Ashton Gillotte is in the midst of a two-game sack streak and Chris Jones has registered 2.5 sacks over the last two games. The Cardinals’ offensive line is a point to watch, as they played against the Rams without starting center Hjalte Froholdt (concussion) and left tackle Jayden Williams (knee), who had already replaced left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. (biceps tear). Both Froholdt and Williams were limited in practice Wednesday. The situation doesn’t get any easier for the Cardinals on the other side of the ball. In the run game, the Cardinals allow 4.2 yards per carry, and through the air, they give up 8.2 yards per pass attempt. The Chiefs opted to rest Kenneth Walker last Sunday against the Falcons because of groin tightness, and he didn’t practice Wednesday . That means rookie Emmett Johnson could make his second straight start after compiling 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in Atlanta. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes is coming off his best passing stat line of the season, in which he threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns against the Falcons. But bigger than that were the chunk gains, as the outing included seven completions of 20 yards or more. While the Cardinals’ secondary is susceptible to explosive passing plays, if there is one area of concern for the Chiefs, it’s that they’re more than capable of generating pressure. Led by safety Budda Baker with 3.5 sacks and outside linebackers Zaven Collins and Josh Sweat with three apiece, the Cardinals have registered 21 sacks this season. “They do a great job of causing havoc and causing pressure, and they do a great job throughout a lot of these football games of kind of stopping the offenses,” Mahomes said. “There’s been parts where offenses have kind of found the big plays, and it has to come within rhythm. It’s not like you can kind of hunt those things. You have to get the ball out of your hand, because if you don’t, they’ll get home, and they’ll cause negative plays.” Protection will be imperative for what could be a shorthanded Chiefs offensive line. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion) both missed practice Wednesday, and it remains to be seen whether newly signed veteran Fred Johnson can provide a boost after joining Kansas City’s practice squad Tuesday. In his opening game in a Kansas City uniform , wide receiver Josh Downs turned 11 snaps into four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown. Wide receiver Rashee Rice led the Chiefs with 82 yards, and Downs, Andrew Armstrong and rookie Cyrus Allen all reached the end zone. Sunday’s game will give way to a short Thanksgiving week for the Chiefs, with perhaps their most important game of the season awaiting them Thursday night against the Buffalo Bills. Given the grand disparity between the two clubs, look for head coach Andy Reid to be mindful about how long he plays some of his key contributors, especially those dealing with injuries. Cardinals-Chiefs game prediction In my 13 years analyzing and previewing Chiefs games, I’m not sure that I can recall a matchup this lopsided going in. But as they say, that’s why they play the games. away.headline: NFL injury news: Cardinals QB Gardner Minshew suffers torn UCL, set for season ending surgery | Report
away.source: The Sunday Guardian Live on MSN
away.blurb: India, Nov. 15 -- Arizona Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew is set to undergo season-ending surgery after suffering a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his throwing elbow. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported on November 15 that Minshew is planning to have the surgery, although he is still working on the timing of the procedure. The injury is a major setback for the Cardinals, who have already placed the veteran quarterback on Injured Reserve. Minshew's 2026 campaign is officially over, leaving rookie Carson Beck to take charge of Arizona's quarterback room. Gardner Minshew To Undergo Surgery After Torn UCL Injury According to Schefter, Minshew is expected to undergo surgery to address the torn UCL in his right elbow. While the quarterback has not finalised when he will have the procedure, he is planning to go ahead with the operation. The injury occurred during Arizona's Week 9 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks on November 8. Seahawks linebacker Dante Fowler Jr. hit Minshew during his throwing motion on the final play of the first half, forcing a fumble. Minshew immediately appeared to be in discomfort but surprisingly returned after halftime and completed the game. He finished the contest with 21 completions on 30 attempts for 166 passing yards. However, the Cardinals suffered a 17-3 defeat against Seattle. Cardinals Place Gardner Minshew On Injured Reserve The Arizona Cardinals officially placed Minshew on Injured Reserve on November 10, confirming that he would miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Before suffering the injury, Minshew had completed 38 of 53 passes for 354 yards and three touchdowns across two appearances for Arizona. His brief stint with the Cardinals included an impressive performance against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Coming off the bench, Minshew threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns, helping Arizona secure a dramatic 33-30 overtime victory. His performance earned him the starting quarterback position, but his promotion was followed by the devastating elbow injury. Carson Beck Takes Over As Cardinals Starting Quarterback With Minshew sidelined, rookie quarterback Carson Beck is expected to lead the Cardinals' offence. Arizona has also strengthened its quarterback depth by signing veteran Josh Johnson and rookie Joey Aguilar. Johnson joined from the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad, while Aguilar arrived from the Jacksonville Jaguars' practice squad. The Cardinals are now relying on their rookie quarterback to navigate the remainder of a challenging season. Minshew's injury also creates uncertainty surrounding his future in Arizona, as the veteran quarterback is scheduled to become a free agent after the 2026 campaign. For now, the priority will be his recovery following surgery as the Cardinals look to move forward without their experienced signal caller.
