It seems the Pro Bowl tight end is on track to play against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. However, it should be interesting to see if he’s limited on snaps or if Patrick Mahomes targets him less as Kansas City navigates any further aggravation of the high ankle sprain he suffered last month. The Kansas City Chiefs had a brief injury scare during this past Sunday’s win over the Atlanta Falcons as 11-time Pro Bowl tight end Travis Kelce limped off the field in the first quarter. There was concern about an aggravation of a right high-ankle sprain Kelce suffered last month against the Los Angeles Chargers. Against the Falcons, the concern arose after Kelce caught a 23-yard pass and was tackled by safety DeMarcco Hellams. During the “ New Heights Podcast ” on Wednesday, Jason Kelce brought up a fan comment that suggested Hellams’ hit on Travis Kelce was “an intentionally dirty tackle targeting the area they knew was injured from the report.” Jason Kelce indicated that from watching the replay “it was hard to tell if there was intentionalness there,” and his brother agreed with his sentiment. More news: Andy Reid Provides Update on Travis Kelce’s Ankle Injury “I don’t know if that was the case; the way he tackled me … and I just got caught in a bad position,” Travis Kelce said. “You know that’s football, and on the flip side, you know, if it was a quote-unquote intentional extra turn and grab of the ankle, you know it’s just a part of it. I don’t think it was crazy enough for it to get a flag or be a fine or anything like that. “Obviously, in the moment, I thought it was, because it hurt like hell,” he added. Jason Kelce added that the reader brought up an interesting point about how teams have to disclose which body part of a player is injured on injury reports. The reader indicated that the NHL often has “upper body injury” or “lower body injury” rather than the exact body part on teams’ injury reports. home.blurb: Wiley was carted to the locker room during the first quarter of the blowout win over the Falcons. The team dealt with a few more injuries as the game went on. Reid confirmed that Creed Humphrey got poked in the eye, which was clear on TV. He finished the game and will ultimately be ok. As for CB Mansoor Delane, it seems like he was pulled more so out of an abundance of caution. "He landed on his back and kind of up on that shoulder area," Reid said. "I think he was scared more than anything. He's going to be alright, though." Another injury setback for Delane's shoulder would be troubling, but he sounds like he avoided anything serious. As for Wiley, this is the type of injury that could prematurely end his Chiefs career. As a rookie out of TCU in 2024, Wiley suffered a season-ending ACL injury during practice. That injury really took away the remainder of his rookie season and limited him during the 2025 NFL season as well. It wasn't until this offseason that he felt like he was getting back to himself. However, that never really came to fruition in on-field production. Now, with the ankle fracture that will almost certainly end his season, Wiley is heading for another long rehab and recovery. A fourth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft out of TCU, Wiley is listed at 6-foot-6 and 250 pounds. The Chiefs have appeared in 50 combined regular-season and postseason games since the start of the 2024 NFL season. Whether it has been injury or a healthy scratch, Wiley has played in 15 of 50 possible games during that timeframe. Wiley is likely slated for IR with the fractured ankle, with eight more games left in the 2026 NFL regular season. As for how the team will adapt to Wiley's loss, it likely opens a needed roster spot, with Omarr Norman-Lott slated to return soon . Kansas City has three tight ends on the 53-man roster currently, with Travis Kelce, Noah Gray, and Jake Briningstool. They have one tight end on the practice squad in the International Player Pathway Program, Thomas Odukoya. picks.headline: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Giannis red hot vs. Bucks Boone's trade charts Cowboys DC latest Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) head to Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday for a game against their instate rival, the Philadelphia Eagles (2-7). Although on the road, this game comes at a critical point in the Steelers’ season. With games the next three weeks against the Broncos, the Texans, and the Jaguars - all teams contending for a playoff spot in the AFC - this one is a near must-win against the Birds. Second in the AFC North and sixth in the AFC overall, Aaron Rodgers and co. are a half-game ahead of the Browns and 1.5 games ahead of the Patriots in the postseason chase. The Eagles have struggled for most of the season. Jalen Hurts led Philly to wins in their first two games, but the Eagles have since lost every game as well as their quarterback (blood clots). This season, the Steelers have leaned on Rodgers, a productive running game and a defense that ranks among the league leaders in sacks and turnover differential. The veteran signal-caller has thrown for 2,014 yards with 15 touchdowns and six interceptions, while Jaylen Warren has rushed for 719 yards. Philadelphia’s season has unraveled in large part because of injuries, most notably the aforementioned loss of Hurts to injured reserve with blood clots. That leaves Joe Milton III directing an Eagles offense averaging just 16.4 points and an NFL-low 260.2 yards per game. Pittsburgh’s four-game winning streak came to an abrupt end last Sunday in a 38-18 road loss to Cincinnati. The Bengals completely suffocated the Steelers with Pittsburgh managing only 23 total yards through the first three quarters before producing some offense and points after the game was out of reach. DK Metcalf was held without a catch through three quarters before finishing with two receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown, while the defense spent far too much time on the field. Philadelphia, meanwhile, comes into Sunday’s game rested after its bye but desperately searching for an answer to a disastrous stretch. The Eagles’ most recent game was a 19-11 home loss to the Giants on Nov. 8. Milton made his first Eagles start and completed 18 of 34 passes for just 169 yards. It has been a weekly headline for Philadelphia: “Eagles’ are Offensive on Offense”. The bye, though, may help an injury-ravaged roster: receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could return after missing the Giants game. Smith’s availability is especially significant because the Eagles badly need another proven weapon alongside Saquon Barkley to make life easier for Milton against a Pittsburgh defense featuring T.J. Watt and one of the NFL’s better pass rushes. Beyond Pittsburgh’s attempt to rebound and Philadelphia’s effort to stop its seven-game skid, the matchup carries a fascinating piece of Pennsylvania rivalry history. The Eagles lead the all-time series 50-29-3, and Pittsburgh has endured an extraordinary drought in Philadelphia. The Steelers have not won in Philly since 1965. They have lost their last 11 games against the Eagles in the City of Brotherly Love. Philadelphia has also dominated the two most recent meetings, winning 27-13 in Philadelphia on Dec. 15, 2024, after a 35-13 home victory in 2022; Pittsburgh’s last win in the series was a 38-29 victory at Heinz Field in 2020. Let’s dive further into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. away.headline: Steelers receive huge injury update on promising young WR
away.blurb: Fans of the Pittsburgh Steelers rejoice! The Aaron Rodgers -led offense may have looked completely outclassed in last week's blowout loss, but the team is on the verge of receiving some much-needed wide receiver help ahead of their Week 11 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles . According to head coach Mike McCarthy, wide receiver Roman Wilson, who has missed the past four games after dislocating his finger back in Week 5, had his 21-day IR practice window opened as he returned to practice on Wednesday. Wilson, who was drafted by the Steelers in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft, had a slower-than-usual start than fans have grown accustomed to when it comes to Pittsburgh's history of finding elite Day 2 wide receivers. While Wilson didn't have that much of a role during his first two years in the league, he has become one of Rodgers' favorite targets in 2026, recording 14 catches for 188 yards and two touchdowns in five games. It remains to be seen if Wilson can be activated off injured reserve in time for the Week 11 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles, but we at Steelers Wire will monitor his status closely via the team's official injury reports. away.headline: Pittsburgh Steelers cut ties with former Giants wide receiver
away.blurb: The Pittsburgh Steelers have cut ties with wide receiver Isaiah Hodgins , who was on the practice squad with the team since Week 2. Hodgins was added when Max Hurleman went down with a hamstring injury, but with Hurleman’s return, the team has decided to move on. A sixth-round pick out of Oregon State by the Buffalo Bills, Hodgins has experience playing outside and in the slot with the teams. He has 70 receptions for 749 receiving yards and eight touchdowns in his career. Hurleman along with Brandon Johnson still remain on the Steelers’ practice squad. The Steelers have seen Hurleman earn some praise over the last week with Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy giving him notable praise. Hodgins never was elevated from the practice squad, unlike Johnson and Brandon Smith. Smith remains on the 53-man roster. Hodgins was with the Steelers last year but the Giants signed him off the practice squad. The Giants moved on from Hodgins earlier this year before he landed with the Steelers. Hodgins spent his first three seasons in the NFL with the Bills, but was cut in the middle of 2022 when the Giants claimed him off waivers. He would spent the next three years there until the expiration of his rookie contract. Standing at 6-foot-4, Hodgins has unique size for the position. His father, James, was a fullback and that gives him a level of experience around the game since the time he was a kid. His brother played defensive line at Oregon State. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit pennlive.com. Distributed by Tribune Content Agency, LLC.

away.headline: Ravens activate RB Adam Randall from injured reserve
away.blurb: The Ravens now have four IR activations remaining with two more available if they miraculously make the playoff. One is reserved for quarterback Lamar Jackson, and another could be bookmarked for kicker Tyler Loop. When center Jovaughn Gwyn went down in Week 3 with knee injury, there was some hope that he could come back at some point but no updates since. The same is true of second-year cornerback Bilhol Kone, who was designated for return when he was placed on IR during roster cuts but has yet to return to practice. Baltimore also needs to consider the possibility of key players going down in the next few weeks, which could require IR stints before late-season returns. Randall, 22, landed on injured reserve at the end of the preseason with a foot injury. What was initially suspected to be an IR stash for a young player turned out to be a more serious issue that sidelined him until Week 8. Randall returned to practice on October 28 as a full participant, but the Ravens used his full three-week practice window to preserve roster flexibility as they navigated injuries and the trade deadline. The Baltimore Ravens activated running back Adam Randall from injured reserve on Wednesday, possibly positioning the sixth-round pick to make his NFL debut on Sunday against the Panthers. Baltimore’s run game has been stagnant for weeks, so Randall could prove some juice as a change-of-pace back. However, he is unlikely to do much better than Derrick Henry behind a struggling offensive line. Randall’s ability to contribute in the pass catching game is unlikely to be utilized given the presence of Justice Hill. However, he is no guarantee to be part of the game day picture with Rasheen Ali entrenched on special teams. As the Ravens’ season slips further and further away, they should consider giving Randall more time. His age, size, and athleticism offer an appealing developmental trajectory that could elevate him to at least a No. 2 role in the backfield while on his rookie contract. The Ravens also re-signed guard Michael Jordan to the practice squad as additional offensive line depth. He fills the spot opened by kicker Harrison Mevis’ release on Tuesday. Riley Patterson hit all four of his kicks – two short field goals and two extra points – in his team debut on Monday night, likely securing him the kicking job until Tyler Loop comes off IR.

away.headline: NFL fans react to Ravens’ rumored plan for Lamar Jackson’s return after thumb injury
away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens believe Lamar Jackson has a chance to return from his broken right thumb for their Week 16 game against the Cleveland Browns on Dec. 27 if his rehab goes smoothly, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported this week. Lamar Jackson’s Road From Buffalo Toward a Possible Browns Return In a statement the team released that day, head coach Jesse Minter called recovery timelines “challenging to predict” and said, “He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.” Minter added, “We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season.” Graziano’s report hinges on Jackson’s progress in the same way, leaving the Browns game at M&T Bank Stadium a possibility rather than a set date for his return. For another fan, the calendar is the problem, since a return against the Browns would leave Jackson only two more regular-season games after that one. A Dec. 27 return would be near the optimistic end of Jackson’s reported recovery timetable, though the Ravens have emphasized that his progress, rather than a fixed date, will determine when he can play again. The report comes with Baltimore at 4-6, days after a 23-20 home loss to the Los Angeles Chargers, who had not won a game before Monday night. Despite the prospect of Jackson returning for the final stretch of the regular season, several fans who responded to the report argued that the Ravens should keep him sidelined and focus on having him healthy for 2027. Jackson’s injury came on Baltimore’s first offensive play of the Nov. 1 game at Buffalo, a 36-10 loss, when his throwing hand caught the arm of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau as he threw. On Nov. 13, the Ravens said the thumb was dislocated and broken and that the injury typically carries a recovery of six to 10 weeks. The Ravens sit fourth in the AFC North and have lost five straight games, including the Buffalo game in which Jackson was hurt and both games since. Jacoby Brissett, whom Baltimore acquired in a trade, started in Jackson’s place in the loss to the Chargers. “It’s already over … just take the rest of the season off,” another fan responded. Jackson’s health is another piece of it. A high ankle sprain had already cost him three games before the thumb injury, and he has played just 14 full quarters this season. A fan pointed to that history: “Yea bro let’s have Lamar play meaningless games in a lost season after 2 major injuries.” Others looked straight ahead to next season. “What’s the point to play him at that point, come back ’27 stronger,” one fan wrote. The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. They kept it competitive for a little more than a half. At halftime the Jets trailed 10 – 6. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 – 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. The Bills outscored the Jets 21 – 3 the rest of the way as Klubnik and the Jets offense were no match for Josh Allen and the Bills offense. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. The Jets are also just one loss away from their 11th straight losing season. The last time the Jets won more than seven games in a season Barack Obama was still President. Now the Jets go on the road to face the only winless team left in the NFL, the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers play the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, so it's possible they will no longer be winless by the time they face the Jets. The Chargers rank dead last in the NFL in points scored, with Justin Herbert somehow crashing to by far the lowest point in his career. After spending his entire career in the vicinity of a top 10 quarterback in the NFL, Herbert has arguably been the worst starting quarterback in the league this year. New Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels' system appears to be a poor match for Herbert's skill set, and the result has been an offensive train wreck. The Chargers have not scored more than 23 points in any game this season, and they have not allowed less than 22 points in any game this season. away.headline: Geno Smith: 'The Plan' Is to Let This Week Unfold, Then Return as Jets' Starter at LA
away.blurb: It starts with the quarterback's attitude regarding some injuries, -- "just normal football stuff," that he experienced against Buffalo. He's on the Jets' injury report, listed as limited for Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury, but he foresees having the ball back in his hands so he can operate the offense against the Chargers on Sunday. "It's football. It comes with it," he said of the play, which wasn't flagged by the officials. "If they throw a flag, they do, it they don't, they don't. My job is to go out there and play and not worry about it." "My job is to be coachable and be the player, and I respect Coach Glenn and everything that he says," Smith said. "He makes the calls, so I'll do as I've always done. When I was a backup for years, I prepared as if I was the starter, and nothing changes for me. ... I do appreciate Coach going out and saying that. He doesn't have to say that, but I do appreciate it." home.headline: Jets’ Geno Smith gets injury update ahead of Chargers clash
home.blurb: As the Jets prepare for a critical Week 11 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers, aiming to end a painful five-game losing streak, all eyes are on Smith's practice availability. In an update from Florham Park, veteran ESPN beat reporter Rich Cimini provided clarity on Smith's participation: "QB Geno Smith (ankle) will be limited today, per Glenn." Smith's limited participation in practice is a positive sign, especially after he required X-rays at the stadium and was seen leaving MetLife Stadium on a golf cart following Sunday's defeat. Despite Smith's modest performance, completing 13 of 21 passes for 148 yards before his exit against Buffalo, head coach Aaron Glenn quickly dismissed any talk of a quarterback controversy between Smith and Klubnik. In a videoconference with reporters, Glenn firmly stated, "Geno's our starter. Come on now, let's not do that. I think Geno's had a really good year, and it would be disrespectful to him to just [replace him]." With Smith returning to practice, even in a limited capacity, the Jets are clearly counting on their established QB1 to lead the offense this Sunday. home.blurb: Breaking Down Jets' Injury Outlook to Begin Week 11 (Who's Hurt & Who Could Return vs. Chargers) - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Because of the NFL's aggressive and physical nature, it's nearly impossible for a team to finish a game without a player suffering an injury. While injuries are part of the game, some teams sustain more injuries than others, which ultimately affects how their season plays out. Omar Cooper Jr. sustained an ankle injury on the first play and didn't return to the game. Dylan Parham and Geno Smith also suffered injuries and were unable to return. Even though Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was listed as a limited participant on Friday, he was ruled out against the Bills with an illness. The former Louisville Cardinal has had an up-and-down season, recording 11 total tackles and a sack across eight games. If Brownlee is either a full or limited participant in the Jets' upcoming practices, we should expect him to play against the Chargers. Since re-injuring his quad in Week 6 against the Patriots, Mauigoa has been on injured reserve, but he is eligible to return for Week 11's matchup with the Chargers. The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt reported Friday that Mauigoa was one of seven players on injured reserve who were working out off to the side of practice . This doesn't mean Mauigoa will play next Sunday, but his appearance at practice indicates that he's ramping up and getting closer to making a return. Trevin Wallace was the only player who didn't participate in any of the Jets' practices last week and, as a result, was ruled out for Week 10's matchup due to a groin injury. Although the injury has sidelined him for the past two weeks, it hasn't had major consequences for New York's special teams. Even though Wallace hasn't impressed in this role, recording just three total tackles and earning a 63.9 special teams grade , per Pro Football Focus , the team could use all the contributors it can get after allowing a 95-yard kickoff return for a touchdown to Dylan Laube two weeks ago. If Wallace can be a full participant in any of the team's practices this week, we should anticipate his return to the lineup next Sunday. If Smith is available and practices during the week, we should expect the 14-year veteran to suit up. But if he doesn't, New York will turn to rookie Cade Klubnik as its starter.Although Klubnik showed some flashes, he needs more time and reps before he can be a reliable starter. They currently sit at 7-2, are in the hunt for the AFC West title and the top seed in the AFC. Even better is the week off should allow the Broncos to get players back from injury, especially on defense. All of this to say Denver is in a great spot. Now come the hated Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, led by rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. The Broncos want to build on this great start to the season and carry the momentum over from the bye this Sunday against their rivals. Denver is a massive -10-point home favorite against the Raiders (4-6) at FanDuel Sportsbook. The total sits at over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the under at -115. Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Just win, baby! (By starting fast offensively) The best way to put pressure on a rookie quarterback is to make the Las Vegas offense one-dimensional. Bo Nix and the Broncos offense can do their part by starting Sunday's game fast offensively and finishing drives with touchdowns. We saw glimpses of this against the Carolina Panthers, with some deep shots early by Nix, but Denver had to kick a field goal on the opening drive. Replicate that this Sunday, but finish the opening drive with a touchdown. And then do it again. And then again. Add to the pressure that the Broncos defense will undoubtedly bring on the rookie QB. — Ian St. Clair Get after Fernando Mendoza Last week, Fernando Mendoza got his first career NFL start against a fierce Seattle Seahawks defense. Prior to Mendoza being a starter, the Raiders' offensive line only allowed 11 sacks when Kirk Cousins was quarterback. Last Sunday, with the 2026 NFL Draft's top pick under center, they gave up six to the Seahawks. If Denver wants to win the game, their defensive front seven has to dominate. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph needs to throw everything he can at the rookie signal caller and rattle him early and often. — Christopher Hart Keep feeding Jonah Coleman I don't need to discuss numbers. Just look at how much better the offense is when Coleman gets his touches. Whether he's running the ball or catching passes, he gives the offense a weapon that forces the defense to respect what Denver is doing in the trenches, thus opening up the opportunities for Bo Nix to push the ball downfield. — Adam Malnati Blow a team out for once I know, I know. It's just not how this team is built. Every team gets a chance to beat the Broncos, but most of them fail to do so in the final minutes. Buuuuut, it would sure be nice to enjoy a good ol' fashioned butt-whoopin' type game — especially against the Raiders. — Tim Lynch Score more points than the Raiders The Broncos scored more points than the Panthers a few weeks ago and didn't need to score any last week, because they were on a bye. Now, it's Raiders week, and my key to the game is simple. Score more points than the Raiders. Denver is 7-0 when it does that and 0-2 when it does not. Using advanced analytics, I say the Broncos have a 100% chance to win on Sunday if they score more points than the Raiders. home.headline: Raiders brace for bad news on star tight end ahead of Broncos showdown
home.blurb: Tight end Brock Bowers missed Wednesday’s practice with the ankle injury that knocked him out of the Raiders’ 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. Coach Klint Kubiak said Bowers was progressing but remained day-to-day. Bowers has not been ruled out against Denver. His absence Wednesday does, however, leave Las Vegas preparing for an AFC West road game without knowing how much its most productive pass catcher can contribute. Bowers injured his ankle while blocking early against Seattle. He returned briefly but was ruled out for the second half, as he finished with two catches for 18 yards. The Raiders offense declined sharply after its promising start. The Las Vegas Raiders opened preparations for Sunday’s game the Denver Broncos without their top target in practice. The Raiders are 4-6 after consecutive losses. Denver, 7-2 and tied for first in the AFC West, returns from its bye riding a five-game winning streak. Fernando Mendoza will make his second career start against a defense that ranks among the NFL ’s top 10 in sacks, pressures and quarterback hits. Bowers leads Las Vegas with 50 catches, 676 receiving yards and six touchdown receptions. Losing him would remove the offense’s leader in all three categories while Mendoza is still adjusting to starting in the NFL. Mendoza completed 11 of 13 passes for 90 yards before halftime and scored on a 10-yard run. Seattle eventually sacked him six times. After a second-quarter field goal, the Raiders punted on seven straight possessions and gained just 24 yards over that stretch. Kubiak acknowledged that losing Bowers affected the offense, but he put responsibility for finding other ways to move the ball on himself. “So I look at myself,” Kubiak said. “I have to do a much better job of moving the ball and spreading the ball around.” Denver presents another difficult assignment. Its defense has allowed 20.7 points per game, ninth in the league, and has recorded 26 sacks. The Raiders have averaged only 70.7 rushing yards per game, ranking 31st, so the ground game isn’t easing the pressure on a young quarterback. Wednesday’s update leaves Bowers’ availability unresolved. Las Vegas can get him back before Sunday’s 1:25 p.m. PT kickoff, but Mendoza and Kubiak cannot yet count on having their leading receiver against the Broncos. picks.headline: Behind Enemy Lines: Previewing the Jaguars' Matchup With Giants, J.J. McCarthy, and More
picks.blurb: Behind Enemy Lines: Previewing the Jaguars' Matchup With Giants, J.J. McCarthy, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the Jacksonville Jaguars, this is a big one. The Jaguars are set to face their toughest test since the bye week ended with the 5-3-1 New York Giants in Week 11. A game that head coach Liam Coen has already said will have to be won in the trenches will be a challenge the Jaguars haven't faced in Weeks. To preview the Jaguars and Giants clash as Jacksonville prepares for their second-half playoff run, we spoke with Patricia Traina of Giants OnSI to go behind the scenes and get an idea of what the Jaguars can really expect. So, how does Traina see this game from the Giants' perspective, and what will it take for Jacksonville to win? We break it down below. 1) What is Arvell Reese more dangerous at: playing linebacker or rushing the passer? Traina: Both. Overall, Reese ranks third among Giants linebackers (inside and outside) with 14 pressures per NFL+, and he has the second-lowest average time to sack (4.0 seconds) in that group. And the scary thing is that this young man, whose name has been mentioned for Defensive Rookie of the Year honors, is just getting started. Reese as a pass rusher (just 107 times so far) as he has been in coverage (246 times). I would think that as the game continues to slow down for him, he will see an increase in his role. 2) How do you view the matchup between Malik Nabers and Travis Hunter? Traina: I think that’s going to be a key matchup. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy has done a good job of scheming Nabers open this season by moving him around the formation. When playing in the slot, he has an 84.6% reception rate and has scored both of his touchdowns from the slot. Travis Hunter hasn’t worked much from the slot this season. They have Hunter down as having played six total snaps in the slot, defending just one target that was not completed. I am very interested in seeing how much the Giants put Nabers in the slot on Sunday and, when he’s not in the slot, how much, if any, the Jaguars have Hunter travel with him. 3) How much have the Giants trusted J.J. McCarthy when it comes to attacking defenses downfield? Explosive plays have been one of the Jaguars’ few weaknesses. Traina: Overall, the Giants have a 44.7% passing completion rate (10th in the league) on deep balls of 20+ air yards. This season, McCarthy has a 52.6% completion rate on deep passes of 20+ air yards. As you might guess, Nabers has been the main target on those deep balls., he’s caught 12 of 21 (57.1%) with one drop. Rookie Malachi Fields has caught three of nine, and Darnell Mooney one of six. Tight end Isaiah Likely has caught three of seven deep passes. As I’m guessing the Jaguars will do everything possible to take Nabers out of the equation, I suspect this could be a good opportunity for Fields to have a breakout game. 4) What kind of impact has former Jaguars CB Greg Newsome made in New York? Traina: He’s been outstanding in coverage, so much so that the Giants recently gave him a three-year contract extension. He currently has a career-best 71.2 coverage grade from PFF and has allowed opponents just a 57.6% completion rate. Newsome has also allowed just 61 YAC, has yet to surrender a touchdown, and has five pass breakups, all good for a 63.8 NFL coverage rating, which is the best of his career. 5) If Jacksonville wins this game, what do you think would be the biggest reason why? They make the Giants one-dimensional. The Jaguars have one of the best run defenses in the league right now, and I’m fairly certain they’ll zero in on shutting down running back Cam Skattebo and challenging McCarthy to beat them through the air. McCarthy is 9-4 as a starter in games where his offense has rushed for 100+ yards collectively. That’s not to say McCarthy and the Giants can’t pull off the upset, but if they become one-dimensional, it’ll be that much harder for them to do so. As my readers and listeners have reminded me, the Giants ran up a storm against the Houston Texans a few weeks back, posting a season-high 188 yards against a Texans run defense that was top five going into that game. So yes, the Giants have a chance. Published 1 hour ago JOHN SHIPLEY John Shipley has been covering the Jacksonville Jaguars as a beat reporter and publisher of Jaguar Report since 2019. picks.blurb: NFL Week 11 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Jaguars blow past Giants, Vikings stay hot with Kirk Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites Anaheim Ducks Boston Bruins Buffalo Sabres Calgary Flames Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Blackhawks Colorado Avalanche Columbus Blue Jackets Detroit Red Wings Edmonton Oilers Florida Panthers Los Angeles Kings Minnesota Wild Montreal Canadiens Nashville Predators New Jersey Devils New York Islanders New York Rangers Ottawa Senators Philadelphia Flyers Pittsburgh Penguins San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken St. Louis Blues Tampa Bay Lightning Toronto Maple Leafs Vancouver Canucks Vegas Golden Knights Washington Capitals Winnipeg Jets COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact FanSided Network Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites I'm not going to lie to you, NFL Week 11 isn't exactly loaded with marquee matchups. Teams like the Chicago Bears , Buffalo Bills , Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos — you know, the contenders in this league right now — are all matched up with teams well out of the playoff race. Throw in the fact that six teams are on bye, and the schedule gets leaner. But we do have two big-time matchups with the Jacksonville Jaguars visiting the New York Giants and then a huge Sunday Night Football showdown in Mexico City with the Minnesota Vikings taking on the San Francisco 49ers for NFC supremacy. But regardless of the quality of matchup, we have every game covered in our NFL picks and predictions. We're coming off of two winning weeks in a row and are getting our mojo back. Surely a week in which there are numerous double-digit spreads with heavy and deserved favorites won't come back to haunt us. But here we go, once again delivering with NFL picks for Week 11 with predictions for every game straight-up and against the spread. NFL Week 11 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington, quarterback Trevor Lawrence | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 11 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Colts vs. Texans (TNF) Saints vs. Bears Ravens vs. Panthers Panthers -2.5 Dolphins vs. Bills Titans vs. Cowboys Cardinals vs. Chiefs Buccaneers vs. Lions Buccaneers +6.5 Steelers vs. Eagles Steelers -4.5 Jets vs. Chargers Raiders vs. Broncos Jaguars vs. Giants Vikings vs. 49ers (SNF) Bengals vs. Commanders 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 95-57 (Last week 11-3) | ATS Record: 71-78-3 (Last week 9-5) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 11 prediction to make Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Minnesota Vikings (+3) vs. San Francisco 49ers – in Mexico City Minnesota Vikings (+3) vs. San Francisco 49ers – in Mexico City Point blank, these are two of the three best teams in the NFC right now. So you throw in the fact that this game is at a neutral site in primetime and it makes it even more difficult. Looking at these two teams, though, people are going to look at the 49ers and their high-powered offense and be intrigued by that. But the Vikings have proven that, under Brian Flores, they're capable of slowing down anyone. Heck, the Lions and Packers both found that out — even if the Detroit got the win thanks to Kyler Murray. But now Kirk Cousins is back in the fold for Minnesota and we've seen him already step in and raise the baseline of the Vikings offense substantially. Who knew getting Justin Jefferson the ball was the smart play? It's that end of the field that ended up being my deciding factor here, though. The fact that the Vikings offense has found this new level of competency complements the defense so incredibly well. Moreover, the 49ers defense, though talented, hasn't exactly been infallible of late. So in Mexico City, give me the Vikings staying hot and establishing a foothold in the NFC. Easiest NFL Week 11 pick on the board Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III, quarterback Caleb Williams | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5) New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5) This feels scarily too easy. Like, have oddsmakers watched the Saints recently? This defense is struggling mightily right now and the offense isn't exactly lighting the world on fire anymore either. To add to that, the Bears have been clinical more often than not this season (the last time out against the Buccaneers where Caleb Williams couldn't stop throwing picks, notwithstanding). Now we get Ben Johnson and this team coming out of a bye where they've had time to gameplan and get healthier. Yeah, that's all lining up pretty heavily toward Chicago for me, especially with this game being played in the Windy City. It's not that I think this game will end up being just a mauling on the Bears' part (though that's also not out of the question). The Saints should be able to score a bit. But it feels like Chicago will just have more consistent and perhaps unstopped success that will ultimately allow them to pull away handily. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6.5) at Detroit Lions Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6.5) at Detroit Lions Yes, I'm aware that Baker Mayfield's health is (once again) in question coming into this game. That's not me saying I have full faith in Jalon Daniels getting back into the offense, though he didn't play that poorly when he had to step in earlier in the season. What I think people are overlooking in this matchup is the fact that the Lions are coming off of the win in Munich and now have to travel back across the country and not get a bye week between games. That has happened for eight teams this season, traveling back from Europe and playing again in one week, and those teams are 2-5-1 straight-up, much less against the spread favored by more than a touchdowns. When you then factor in losing Aidan Hutchinson last week and what that could mean for Detroit's defense — which I wasn't exactly over the moon about to begin with — there's a path here for the Bucs to keep this close. I'll still take the Lions to win straight-up, mainly because I'm a coward and understand they are the substantially better team in this matchup. However, I do think the Buccaneers keep the game within a possession when we get to the end of it. Home / NFL About Pitch a Story Privacy Policy Legal Disclaimer Accessibility Statement

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The New York Giants and Jacksonville Jaguars meet Sunday afternoon at MetLife Stadium in a matchup between two division leaders. New York enters at 5-3-1 and atop the NFC East, while Jacksonville is 7-2 and in first place in the AFC South. The Jaguars have won three straight and emerged as one of the league’s most complete teams, ranking fourth at 29.9 points per game while allowing only 16.0, second-best in the NFL. Trevor Lawrence has thrown for 2,284 yards and 21 touchdowns, while Parker Washington leads Jacksonville with 645 receiving yards. Led by J.J. McCarthy , the Giants have been more modest offensively averaging 22.6 points per game, but their defense ranks among the NFL’s best against the pass, allowing fewer than 200 yards per game. The Giants are trying to bounce back after a painful 24-21 home loss to the Washington Commanders last Thursday. McCarthy completed 23 of 36 passes for 293 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Cam Skattebo ran 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns and Likely exploded for nine catches, 127 yards and a score. This game has been penciled in as a loss for the Giants for weeks now, and it shouldn’t be much of a surprise to anyone paying attention that the 5-3-1 Giants are (nearly) touchdown underdogs to the 7-2 Jaguars. The Giants are coming off of a disappointing, and frustrating, loss to the Washington Commanders, squandering a golden opportunity to put the NFC East in a strangle hold and cement their position as a playoff contender. The Giants had multiple opportunities to put the game away, and instead played to not-lose on offense and defense — only to lose anyway. The Jaguars, meanwhile, are coming off of a 40-23 win over the Tennessee Titans, though that game was closer than the final score until the final 5 minutes or so. One of the biggest questions in the upcoming game is how the Jaguars will incorporate their newly acquired defensive players. The Jags elected to rest NT Jordan Davis and S Jesse Bates, both of whom were acquired in trades last week. DT Devon Godcheaux (acquired from the New Orleans Saints) did play, and ended the game with a tackle. The Giants can find comfort in the fact that they were 10.5-point underdogs on the road to the Houston Texans and came away with a win. away.headline: Jaguars-Titans Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Full-Go Status Puts Focus on Rushing Attack
away.blurb: The Jaguars are set to be without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III against the Titans as the Jaguars give them their bye week, while defensive end BJ Green will also be out as he works his way back from the injured reserve list. Tuten played in last week's game against the Baltimore Ravens despite not practicing that week with a foot/ankle injury, and he also sat out the first two practice days this week. He ended up getting 12 carries for 29 yards and a touchdown a week ago and did participate in Friday's practice as a limited participant, giving him the green light for Sunday against the Titans. The Jaguars had their third-worst rushing performance in terms of EPA/Rush during the 25-game Coen era on Thursday Night Football. Part of this had to do with execution, while another part of it had to do with a run-heavy second-half script after the Jaguars got up on the Ravens at halftime. Add in some bad weather that took the ball out of the hands of the passing game, and the Jaguars' rushing attack had the perfect storm for a regression game. As Coen said, there should be no long-term concerns. But in an AFC where the race for the No. 1 seed will be important week in and week out, and the Jaguars will need their running game to continue hitting its stride over the second-half of the season. home.headline: Giants Cam Skattebo Reveals Backflip Celebration's Future After Aidan Hutchinson's Knee Injury
home.blurb: Cam Skattebo is retiring the backflip. The New York Giants' running back said he will no longer do his signature celebration after seeing Detroit Lions' pass-rusher Aidan Hutchinson tear his ACL during a sack celebration on Sunday. "It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters Monday. "I'm saying yeah [no more backflips]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.' That ain't going to happen to me." He did add that he might bring back the backflip "if we go to the playoffs or something," but acknowledged that Hutchinson "didn't think about [the risk] either, and it happened." You have to think folks with the Giants' organization were jumping for joy—backflipping for joy, even—after hearing Skattebo's comments on the matter.

Otherwise, the only other notable injuries listed by the Giants were safety Jason Pinnock (hip) and outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin). LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 11 picks, including the Jaguars to handle the Giants on the road Imagn Images Stacking winning weeks is always a good feeling when it comes to picking NFL games . I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. Pick: Texans 30, Colts 27 Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. picks.blurb: Vikings vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 11 Sunday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Giannis red hot vs. Bucks Boone's trade charts Cowboys DC latest Vikings vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 11 Sunday Night Football Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Wed, November 18, 2026 at 10:17 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The playoff picture in the NFL is finally starting to come into focus ahead of Week 11. This week's Sunday Night Football matchup features two teams who each in the thick of the NFC playoff race. San Francisco is one of the league's best teams , sitting atop the standings with Buffalo at 8-1 on the season. Minnesota is one game back at 7-2 and fighting for their lives in a wildly competitive NFC North division race. NFL fans will be thrilled at the opportunity to watch San Francisco's offense go up against Minnesota's defense. That marquee matchup alone is the reason why this game has the potential to become an instant classic. But make no mistake, both of these teams are complete in all three phases and have excellent coaching. Something's got to give, and it will be exciting to see which unit takes over this contest. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So who will come out on top in this one? And is the winner of this high-leverage game destined to make the postseason? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this epic Sunday Night Football showdown between the Vikings and 49ers. Brock Purdy does nothing but throw touchdowns, get sacked against elite Vikings defense Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The 49ers are getting plenty of praise this season and rightfully so. But Purdy deserves an even larger slice of that pie than he's currently getting. Purdy is quietly having the best season of his career. He is on pace to surpass his incredible 2023 season in almost every category. If Purdy stays on the same pace, he'll have more passing yards, more touchdowns, and fewer interceptions. Even when zooming out at the whole team, San Francisco went 12-5 in 2023. The 49ers are well ahead of schedule and should finish with a better record this season. Purdy's high level of play has made the difference. So how will he fare against arguably the best NFL defense of the past decade? Purdy will throw at least three touchdown passes against the vaunted Vikings defense. But Purdy won't get away so easy, as Minnesota will extract their pound of flesh too. The Vikings will log at least six sacks throughout this game. Just how bold is this prediction? Purdy has thrown three or more touchdowns three times this season. Meanwhile, the Vikings have put up six or more sacks twice in 2026. Minnesota even had eight sacks last week against Green Bay! The most important part of this prediction is the ratio. Purdy's number of touchdown passes must be exactly half compared to how many times he is sacked. While there is an initial line set, the prediction still holds regardless of how many sacks Purdy takes. Fans for both teams can enjoy tracking the status of this prediction throughout the night. Justin Jefferson has his best game since 2024 against the 49ers What if the legendary Justin Jefferson makes his triumphant return in Week 11? It's not too crazy of a thought with Kirk Cousins throwing him the ball again. Jefferson immediately improved once the Vikings got a capable quarterback under center. Of course, it does help that the pair have a strong relationship after years of playing together. The real question will be whether or not that chemistry can overcome their opponents solid defense. San Francisco's defense is middle of the road in terms of pass coverage. They've allowed 225.7 passing yards per game along with 16 receiving touchdowns in just nine games. The 49ers still have a great defense, but the numbers show that they are far from invincible. Let's assume the real Jefferson does return in Week 11, bringing levels of production not seen since the magical 2024 season. Minnesota's star receiver will log at least 125 receiving yards and at least one touchdown. The last time Jefferson was this productive was Week 16 of the 2024 season against the Seahawks. In that game, Jefferson hauled in 10 receptions for 144 receiving yards and two touchdowns. It's time for that Jefferson to return and guide the Vikings back to the playoffs. 49ers win an overtime thriller against the Vikings Kirby Lee-Imagn Images It will be fascinating to see how each team game plans against the other. Will Minnesota continue to blitz at an absolutely absurd rate against an offensive genius like Kyle Shanahan? And what will San Francisco's plan be for slowing down Kirk Cousins and Minnesota's offense? This game has the potential to turn into either a shootout or a defensive slugfest depending on some of those variables. That level of variability is what makes football so fun to watch. It's tempting to predict a tie in such a tight matchup like this. But both teams have so much to play for that somebody is bound to leave the stadium with a win. The Vikings will do everything they can to force overtime. While they will succeed, the 49ers will come out on top thanks to their superior firepower and coaching advantage. San Francisco prevails on a game-winning field goal. Looking back at NFL's history in Mexico City – NBC Los Angeles Skip to content Main Navigation Search Search for: Local By Logan Reardon • Published November 17, 2026 • Updated on November 17, 2026 at 11:16 am From record-breaking crowds to the first NFL regular-season game outside the United States, Mexico has played a major role in the league’s international expansion. The American football league is heading south of the border in Week 11 to play a game in Mexico City. Stream Los Angeles News for free, 24/7, wherever you are. In a matchup of two of the league's top teams, Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers will face Kirk Cousins and the Minnesota Vikings. The potential NFC Championship Game preview will air on NBC's Sunday Night Football . Before the action gets underway, here’s a full history of the NFL playing in Mexico. Which NFL teams are playing in Mexico in 2026? As aforementioned, the 49ers and Vikings will play in Mexico in Week 11 this season. San Francisco will serve as the designated home team. The game will be played on Sunday Night Football on Nov. 22 at 8:20 p.m. ET (7:20 p.m. local time in Mexico City, 5:20 p.m. PT). How to watch the Vikings-49ers Sunday Night Football game on NBC and Peacock Who is playing in NFL Week 11? Here's the full schedule Which NFL teams have played in Mexico before? In addition to the 49ers and Vikings, only seven other teams have played regular-season games in Mexico: the Las Vegas Raiders, Houston Texans, New England Patriots , Kansas City Chiefs , Los Angeles Chargers and Arizona Cardinals. The 49ers will make their third trip to Mexico, becoming the first team to play there more than two times. The Raiders and Cardinals are the only other teams to play in Mexico twice — the Raiders in 2016 and 2017 and the Cardinals in 2005 and 2022. When was the first NFL game in Mexico? home.blurb: Aiyuk was reinstated by the NFL after spending time on the reserve/left squad list, but the 49ers have yet to release him or add him to their 53-man roster. Florio pointed out that the team has continued to hold onto Aiyuk despite his reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list. “Nine days since Aiyuk was reinstated from the reserve/left squad list, the 49ers haven’t cut him. At this point, with only six days to go, the 49ers surely will kick the can as long as they can. They gain nothing from delaying Aiyuk’s return, other than the relatively minor strategic advantage of keeping him away from a competitor,” Florio said. Florio called out the 49ers for potentially holding Aiyuk back out of spite , describing such a move as “bush-league” and one that would create “bad karma.” He believes the 49ers should let the receiver return to the NFL rather than prolong the situation. “If the 49ers are simply squatting on Aiyuk out of spite, that’s a bush-league move that creates bad karma. Let the guy get back in the league,” Florio said.
